steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the "Computers" section for a Wikipedia article on the 74181 ALU chip: a list of the notable computers and subsystems that were built around it, with a short note on each.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Intro: many CPUs and subsystems based on the 74181
- Data General and DEC machines (Nova, PDP-11, VAX)
- Workstations (Xerox Alto, PERQ)
- Peripheral and floating-point processors (KMC11, FPP-12)
- Other minicomputers, terminals and mainframe options (Computer Automation, Wang, TI, Honeywell, Datapoint, Cogar, Varian, HP, New England Digital)

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- Intro
  - many CPUs/subsystems based on 74181; several historically significant
- Data General / DEC
  - NOVA 1200: Data General, 1970; first commercial 16-bit minicomputer using 74181
    - only one 74181, data run through four times
    - later Nova 800: four 74181s
  - several PDP-11 models; most popular minicomputer of all time; DEC
  - VAX-11/780: first VAX; most popular 32-bit computer of the 1980s; DEC
- Workstations
  - Xerox Alto: first computer with desktop metaphor + GUI
  - Three Rivers PERQ: commercial workstation, influenced by Alto, first released 1979
- Computer Automation Naked Mini LSI-2
  - "LSI" a marketing hook; no LSI processor, four 74181s
- Peripheral / floating point
  - KMC11: peripheral processor for DEC PDP-11
  - FPP-12: floating-point unit for DEC PDP-12
- Others
  - Wang 2200: CPU (one 74181 per CPU), disk controller (two per controller)
  - TI-980A/980B, TI-990: Texas Instruments 16-bit minicomputers
  - Honeywell option 1100: "scientific unit" option, H200/H2000 mainframes
  - Datapoint 2200 Version II: two 74181s; also follow-ons 5500, 6600, 1800/3800; Datapoint = successors of computer that defined Intel 8008 architecture
  - Cogar System 4 / Singer 1501 / ICL 1501 Intelligent Terminal
  - Varian Data Machines V70 series, 16-bit minicomputers
  - HP 2100 series: about half the models used four 74181s
  - New England Digital ABLE 16-bit minicomputer: processor for Synclavier synthesizer, four of the ALU chips

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
A lot of computer CPUs and subsystems were based on the 74181, and some of them are historically significant models.

NOVA 1200: Data General introduced it in 1970 and it was the first commercial 16-bit minicomputer that used the 74181. It only uses one 74181, which is curious, and it runs the data through it four times. The Nova 800, which came later, uses four 74181s.

Several models of the PDP-11. The PDP-11 was the most popular minicomputer of all time and was made by Digital Equipment Corporation.

Xerox Alto: this was the first computer that used the desktop metaphor and a graphical user interface (GUI).

VAX-11/780: this was the first VAX and the most popular 32-bit computer of the 1980s. It was manufactured by Digital Equipment Corp.

Three Rivers PERQ: a commercial computer workstation that was influenced by the Xerox Alto. It was first released in 1979.

Computer Automation Naked Mini LSI-2: the "LSI" here is misused as a marketing hook, since it did not use an LSI processor, it used four 74181s.

- KMC11: peripheral processor for DEC PDP-11
- FPP-12: floating-point unit for DEC PDP-12
- Wang 2200: CPU (one 74181 per CPU), disk controller (two per controller)
- TI-980A/980B, TI-990: TI 16-bit minicomputers
- Honeywell option 1100: "scientific unit" option, H200/H2000 mainframes
- Datapoint 2200 Version II: two 74181s; follow-ons 5500, 6600, 1800/3800; successors of computer that defined Intel 8008 architecture
- Cogar System 4 / Singer 1501 / ICL 1501 Intelligent Terminal
- Varian Data Machines V70 series, 16-bit minicomputers
- HP 2100 series: about half the models used four 74181s
- New England Digital ABLE 16-bit minicomputer, processor for Synclavier, four ALU chips

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
A lot of computer CPUs and subsystems were based on the 74181, and some of them are historically significant models.

NOVA 1200: Data General introduced it in 1970 and it was the first commercial 16-bit minicomputer that used the 74181. It only uses one 74181, which is curious, and it runs the data through it four times. The Nova 800, which came later, uses four 74181s.

Several models of the PDP-11. The PDP-11 was the most popular minicomputer of all time and was made by Digital Equipment Corporation.

Xerox Alto: this was the first computer that used the desktop metaphor and a graphical user interface (GUI).

VAX-11/780: this was the first VAX and the most popular 32-bit computer of the 1980s. It was manufactured by Digital Equipment Corp.

Three Rivers PERQ: a commercial computer workstation that was influenced by the Xerox Alto. It was first released in 1979.

Computer Automation Naked Mini LSI-2: the "LSI" here is misused as a marketing hook, since it did not use an LSI processor, it used four 74181s.

KMC11: this was a peripheral processor for the Digital Equipment Corporation PDP-11.

FPP-12: a floating-point unit for the Digital Equipment Corporation PDP-12.

Wang 2200: the CPU used the 74181 (one per CPU) and so did the disk controller (two per controller).

TI-980A/980B: these are 16-bit minicomputers from Texas Instruments.

TI-990: also 16-bit minicomputers from Texas Instruments.

Honeywell option 1100: this was the "scientific unit" option, as it was called, for the Honeywell H200/H2000 series of mainframes.

Datapoint 2200: Version II used two 74181s, and the follow-on machines did too, the Datapoint 5500, 6600, and 1800/3800. These were the successors of the computer that defined the architecture for the Intel 8008.

Cogar System 4 / Singer 1501 / ICL 1501 Intelligent Terminal.

Varian Data Machines V70 series, which were 16-bit minicomputers.

HP 2100 series: about half of the models in this series used four 74181s.

The ABLE 16-bit minicomputer from New England Digital also used four of these ALU chips. It was used as the processor for the Synclavier synthesizer from the same company.
